newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher Energy sidetracks McKee well.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Energy sidetracks McKee well.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy Ltd said on Thursday it had begun "sidetrack" operations to attempt to increase recovery and production from its McKee oil field in Taranaki, on the west coast of the North Island.
In a weekly drilling report, Fletchers said sidetracking -- branching off an existing drill hole -- of McKee's Toetoe development well started on Wednesday.
Also, the report said as part of a test of the Mangahewa formation the Mangahewa-2 well had been shut in for a 10-day build-up prior to flowing. A hydraulic fracturing programme will start on May 1.
Fletcher believes the whole Mangahewa formation could be bigger than the nearby onshore Kapuni field, the second largest hydrocarbon discovery after offshore Maui.

The Piakau-1 well was closed in for pressure measurements and then opened at low flow rates for a fluids sampling programme. This is part of re-test for hydrocarbon potential of the Tikorangi limestone in the Ahuroa/Piakau prospect.
